reason: Sunlight can evaporate ocean water, beginning the journey into the sky.
expectation: The ocean's water will evaporate or form clouds.

effect: Sun and Ocean produced evaporation, leaving water vapour ready for the next stage of its journey.
reaction: The detail that dissolved salts stay behind was useful.
reason: Air may carry the evaporated water upward, where it can cool and form clouds.
expectation: The vapour will rise and form a cloud.

alternatives.reason: I could check its available partners if the next stage is not as expected.

effect: Evaporation and Air formed Clouds, providing the next stage of the water cycle.
reaction: The distinction between invisible vapour and visible droplets was useful.
reason: Clouds may produce rain when combined with air, as the steam cloud did in the previous chapter.

alternatives.reason: I could check its partners if this chapter handles rainfall differently.

effect: Clouds combined with Water automatically to make Rainfall, so the next step is to bring it onto land.
reaction: I expected Air again; Water was the available partner instead.
reason: Rainfall on the stone crust may begin the flow across land toward rivers.
expectation: Rainfall will gather or flow over the land.

effect: Rainfall on the stone crust created Rivers, which can now carry water and sediment toward the ocean.
reaction: The note that rivers reshape their routes through erosion and deposition was useful.
reason: A river meeting the ocean can deposit sediment and build a delta.
expectation: The rivers will form a delta where they meet the ocean.

effect: Rivers cannot combine directly with Ocean; Earth and Sun are their available partners.
reaction: I expected the river–ocean meeting to make the delta directly.
reason: Earth may supply the sediment rivers need to build a delta.
expectation: The rivers will carry or deposit sediment toward a delta.

alternatives.reason: Sun might help keep water travelling, but Earth seems more relevant to building a delta.

effect: Rivers and Earth produced Sediment, giving me material that may build the delta.
reaction: The connection between erosion upstream and building land elsewhere is useful.
reason: Sediment deposited where rivers meet the ocean can build a delta, so I will try it with the ocean.
expectation: The sediment will accumulate at the coast to form a delta.

alternatives.reason: The rivers might need to carry the sediment further before it forms a delta.

effect: Sediment combined automatically with Rivers to form a Delta, completing that goal. The remaining goal is to keep water travelling.
reaction: I expected Ocean to be the partner, but the river-mouth explanation made the result clear.
reason: Sun is the other known partner for Rivers and may connect the flowing water back to evaporation.
expectation: Sunlight will help return river water to the atmosphere and keep the water cycle moving.

effect: Rivers and Sun created the Water cycle, completing the remaining goal and connecting evaporation, precipitation and runoff.
reaction: It was satisfying to see the separate stages come together, with sunlight and gravity driving different parts.

mostWorthwhile.text: Building sediment and then a delta linked erosion upstream to deposition at a river mouth, making the land-building process tangible.

leastWorthwhile.text: Trying Clouds with Air repeated the previous chapter's apparent pattern, but this chapter required Water instead.

surprise.text: Rivers could not combine directly with Ocean for a delta; they first needed sediment, which then combined with Rivers.

arbitrary.text: Clouds needing Water rather than Air initially felt unclear, though the result explained that additional droplets grow heavy enough to fall.

continue.text: Yes. I would be curious to see more processes connected through making, especially when the explanations clarify how the natural world works.
